title: Frank Netto and Ebby Rao, Owls sidemen
summary: White recalls Frank Netto, trombonist and violinist, who played dinner music at the Edgewater Gulf Hotel. Ebby Rao played with them throughout the spot jobbing, as at a masquerade party at the Chess, Checker and Whist Club.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: You had a song on too.

A trombone player's name that we were trying to think of a minute ago was, well now we can't think of it. Frank Netto. Frank Netto. That's right. I see Frank quite frequently and enjoy his playing so much he's still playing. Frank was a musician, a very fine musician. He played not only trombone but he played violin. He played almost any instrument. He was called upon to do it. I know when we were at the Edgewater Gulf Hotel we had to play a lot of this sweet music for dinner music and he used to put the trombone down and pick up the violin because we had to have a leader that was just supposed to be there, that's all.
Oh Ebby Rao, you're saying you were playing at that chess club?

Chess Checker and Whisk Club. We had a picture there, it was a masquerade party, it was quite a picture. Boy, that goes back a long time. But Ebby played with us all the while we were spotting, spot jobbing. Ebby played with us.
